newsitem.title: LATVIA: British Airways plans Latvia route.
newsitem.headline: British Airways plans Latvia route.

text.p: British Airways plans to start a flight between Britain and the Baltic state of Latvia which it hopes will start operating sometime this summer, a BA manager said on Wednesday.

The route between Riga and London is currently serviced only by Latvian airline Riiair, which has a code-sharing deal with Russia's Transaero, and Air Baltic, which is part-owned by Scandinavian Airlines.
"We have decided that we will fly to Riga subject to getting the necessary route licences from the appropriate authorities," BA Baltics manager Harvey Lines told Reuters.
It would be the first direct BA flight to any of the Baltic states since they regained independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991.
Lines said the airline needed to get the permission of both the British and Latvian aviation authorities to fly between the two countries and also get the slots at Gatwick and Riga airports.
He said BA has already applied for a U.K. licence.
If BA starts the route, it will be the fourth major Western airline after Lufthansa, SAS and Finnair to service Riga.
